record.text: Cross-border projects with Hungarian clients require us to produce deliverables in the Hungarian unified national projection system (EOV), but our Serbian-licensed surveyors are not certified under Hungarian geodetic regulations, which means we must always subcontract the final certification to a Hungarian firm at a cost of roughly 8 percent per project.
record.detail: Hungarian infrastructure clients need deliverables in the EOV projection with Hungarian cadastral reference numbers and a certification stamp from a surveyor licensed under the Hungarian chamber of civil engineers. Our Serbian-licensed staff cannot provide that stamp, even when every measurement was taken by us with our own instruments. The practical result is that on every cross-border project we subcontract the final certification package to a small Hungarian geodetic firm based in Szeged, Térkép és Terep Kft., and we pay them roughly eight percent of project value for review and stamping work that adds no technical content. Over the last financial year that came to approximately 14 000 EUR in margin we handed over. We have looked at whether one of our surveyors could pursue Hungarian chamber registration, but the process requires a Hungarian university degree or a separate recognition procedure that our legal team estimates would take two to three years. What we are looking for is either a faster regulatory path we have not found yet, or a technical and documentation workflow so clean and standardised that it reduces the review time the Hungarian firm charges us for, even if we cannot eliminate the subcontract entirely.
